transcript_segments.text: funny thing the packet says new look same price
less inside which is rude because lately i've been looking suspiciously
new look myself
i picked up a chocolate bar from the corner shop shelf
and thought hang on mate you used to be yourself
same rapper same smile same confident fun
same little promise of exactly what i want
but the thing in my hand felt thin as an excuse
like joy had been ordered for casual use
and i laughed then i didn't because that's been me lately
same face in the glass but the contents feel shady
same name same code same jokes on repeat
but i walk up the stairs and negotiate with my feet
i opened a book i once would've swallowed
and now page three has a hill to follow
i used to catch thoughts like coins from the air
now i pat down my pockets and nothing is there
maybe i'm tired maybe i'm scared
maybe the shelf looks the same but there's less of me there
and my family size with the family gun
same little box with the old weight wrong
they kept the price but they took out the shine
is there a floor to fall in
or is fall in the design
also who decided 27 crisps was a serving
i'd like names but
there was a time i could juggle six tabs in my brain
two conversations and it kept all the pain
i deadline the bill a half written plan
now i lose my keys while they're still in my hand
i read the same sentence nine times in a row
maybe the tenth will agree to come home
i stare at a phone with my blood on my face
and suddenly language had us left the place
things that were easy now asked for a chair
emails arrive and i need medical care
a password reset feels mythic and cruel
a printer says error and i leave the room
and people say that's normal you're just getting older
which is comforting in the way your wet sock is a blanket
because i don't just miss youth
i miss keys i miss opening the door and trusting the keys
i miss being quick without making a speech
i miss feeling the answer
just slightly in reach
and my family sides with the family gone
same little box with the old weight wrong
they kept the price but they took out the shine
is there a floor to fall in
or is falling their design
and i know
everyone says decline is natural
which is true so is mildew
doesn't mean i want it in the corners of my mind
i'm scared there's no bottom that's the bit
not that i'm slower
not that my back now makes noises like an old ship
considering prayer
not that i need recovery time from sitting badly
it's the wandering
is this a dip a season
a warning a receipt
is my brain tied or leaving by degrees
did someone quietly reduce the grams of me
while keeping the packaging neat
and what if i adapt to this smaller version
then wake up next year smaller again
how many losses can you call adjustment
before the word starts looking away
huh
i used to think aging would arrive with a bell
a dramatic little cloak and a story to tell
but it came as small thefts and sensible shoes
a name i misplaced a bruise i didn't choose
a night out requiring three days of repair
a sock on the floor becoming a dare
a sharp little word from someone i love
because my patience ran out with the milk and the gloves
and yes i still laugh i'm not made of glass
i can still make a joke while feeding masks
it gives humour's the trolley with the squeaking wheel
that carries the dread to somewhere less real
but beneath all the bits in the shop floor complaint
there's a kid in my chest saying tell me i ain't
being replaced by a cheaper design
with smaller ideas and a stower mind
maybe i'm less than i was yesterday
or maybe i'm measuring wrong on a terrible day
and my family sighs with the family gone insane
lit the box with the old weight wrong
they cared for price but they took out the shine
is there a flaw to falling or is falling the design
and maybe i'm the smaller maybe that's true
but all the things still hold what they're meant to
for natures small but it knows how to gloat
the seed looks finished till it starts to grow
so yes maybe there's less in the packet
maybe the label lies
maybe i need more rest now
more lists more kindness less pretending
i'm a warehouse with unlimited stock
but i am not empty not yet
it's still something here worth opening
still salt at the bottom still crumbs in the corner
still enough sweetness to make a tired person
stand in the kitchen at midnight
then say alright then one more day
say alright then one more day
